messages:
incident-bot: PAGER — GPU-POOL 'hotpath' at 92% queued; 15m growth; >30% 429s for tier=prod-hot. Paging oncall. Escalation level: production-impact :rotating_light:

maya (oncall): I'm awake, ack. Jumping in now. Any customer-facing pages yet?

leah (support): seeing customer reports from AcmeCorp and Nimbus. Support dashboard shows spikes in 429 and high tail latency. AcmeCorp SLA warnings going out.

raj (infra): quick summary from metrics — autoscaler didn't add new instances after 09:08 UTC. Pool cpu/gpu utilization jumped, queue length 8k -> 18k over 12m. Tokenbucket logs show repeated "reject: rate_exceeded" for token_bucket_id=gpu-hotpath-tier.

maya (oncall): ok. can someone paste the autoscaler & tokenbucket status?

raj (infra): dumping recent state:
```
$ infractl pools status --pool hotpath
pool: hotpath
desired_gpus: 24
allocated_gpus: 24
pending_scale: 0
queue_depth: 18234
autoscaler_state: ACTIVE
autoscaler_last_event: scale_attempt_failed
scale_error: "tokenwindow lock: tier_allocation_unavailable"
```
Tokenbucket snapshot:
```
token_bucket: gpu-hotpath-tier
refill_rate_per_min: 1200
burst: 10000
last_refill: 2026-02-18T09:07:52Z
current_tokens: 0
rejects_1m: 5400
```

toni (sre): that refill_rate looks low for the current mix. Also saw tier-policy logs where prod-hot reserved tokens drained into canary erroneously due to mis-apply of a rate-mapping PR.

maya (oncall): if autoscaler attempted scale and failed due to tokenwindow lock we need to break the lock or open emergency burst. Raj, can you try emergency-burst for hotpath? We'll need to patch tokenbucket or rollback the policy.

raj (infra): applying emergency patch now — increasing refill and bursting to get immediate headroom. Command I'm running:
```
infractl tokenbucket update --id gpu-hotpath-tier --refill-per-min 6000 --burst 40000 --reason "incident emergency burst"
```

ops-bot: ACTION — tokenbucket gpu-hotpath-tier update queued by raj. Change will trigger rolling config push to hotpath nodes.

leah (support): I'm telling AcmeCorp we're aware and working on an emergency mitigation; ETA 6-12min for visible changes per our metrics.

maya (oncall): watch the 429 rate and queue. If we still see >5% customer 429s after config propagate, route top customers to fallback model or dedicated pool.

raj (infra): patch applied. Confirming new snapshot:
```
refill_rate_per_min: 6000
burst: 40000
current_tokens: 35000
rejects_1m: 120
```

maya (oncall): nice. 429s starting to drop — support dashboard shows 429s from 31% -> 9% in last 2 minutes. Latency p95 still high.

toni (sre): autoscaler retry logs show previous scale attempts blocked because tier-policy binding incorrectly marked the hotpath tier as read-only for allocations when a stale rollout flag was set. I removed the flag at 09:18 UTC. Autoscaler now allowed to create new nodes.

raj (infra): autoscaler triggered additional pools, pending nodes 6 -> provisioning -> attached.

ops-bot: DEPLOY — 6 gpu nodes attached to pool hotpath by autoscaler at 09:21 UTC.

leah (support): AcmeCorp reporting degraded but returning to normal, they still saw a handful of failed calls. Filing EMERGENCY-SLA-NOTE for them.

maya (oncall): good. Assigning mitigation tasks: raj follow up to investigate why rate-mapping PR created the leak; toni to validate autoscaler guardrails; leah to coordinate customer comms and impact numbers; I'll start incident timeline.

raj (infra): quick root cause hypothesis: earlier today a tier-policy rollout inadvertently removed a mapping that lets reserved tokens pool across adjacent tiers for short bursts. This made hotpath strictly limited and starved autoscaler handshake which expects token bucket headroom to allow scale operations. I'll fetch the PR and revert the specific change.

maya (oncall): if you have the offending PR number drop it here. Also add a postmortem follow-up tag.

raj (infra): PR #4821 — rollout of rate-mapping v2. Reverting the single change that removed transient cross-tier allowance. Revert command:
```
git revert --no-ff 4821 --author raj
infractl policy apply --policy-rate-mapping default --file reverted-mapping.yaml
```
Applying now.

ops-bot: CHANGE — policy revert started. Will broadcast when applied cluster-wide.

toni (sre): note for postmortem: we need an autoscaler hard-check that disallows scale fail modes when tokenbucket reports 'lock' state; autoscaler should degrade gracefully by shifting lower-priority routes, not fail to scale. Adding JIRA INFRA-1298.

leah (support): impact numbers — between 09:05–09:20 UTC: 4.2% of prod requests got 429s, 0.8% error rate spike affecting 38 unique customers, top affected: AcmeCorp (21k failed requests).

maya (oncall): thanks. We're at steady state now: queue depth 2.2k, allocated_gpus 30, rejects_1m 18. Closing active mitigation. Moving to post-incident review channel in 30m.

raj (infra): confirmed revert applied, token mapping restored. I'll run a replay test to validate no regressions.

maya (oncall): handoff to toni for oncall wrap; I'll prepare initial incident summary for the incident timeline doc and set severity to Sev2 (customer-impacting but recovered).

toni (sre): taking handoff. I'll run through checklist and coordinate the postmortem owner.

leah (support): sending proactive update to affected customers with mitigations and next steps.

maya (oncall): final notes: root cause — tier-policy misconfiguration removed transient cross-tier token allowances causing tokenbucket starvation during a sudden traffic spike; mitigation included emergency tokenbucket refill, autoscaler guard removal, and policy revert. Follow-ups: tighten rollout checks (infra), autoscaler failmode change (sre), customer postmortem (support).

ops-bot: INCIDENT CLOSED (mitigated) — incident ID: INC-20260218-0043 — mitigation timestamp: 3165004540. Please add postmortem notes to /wiki/incidents/INC-20260218-0043. :white_check_mark:
